title: Invitation rate-limits + domain reputation blocking for org/team admin controls
creator: Lena Park
description: Implement layered protections for organization and team invitations: (1) invitation rate-limiting and burst controls for admins to prevent mass invites, (2) domain reputation / blocklist checks against an allowlist/denylist during invite creation, and (3) audit log entries and alerting for suspicious invite patterns. This ticket delivers server-side enforcement and audit integration; a separate design ticket will cover Console UX for admin policy configuration.
background: We currently allow org admins to invite users with only basic denylist checks. Customer incidents and red-team exercises found two gaps: automated scripts can mass-invite addresses causing churn and billing noise, and attackers can use disposable or low-reputation domains that bypass our simple pattern checks. RBAC-v2 introduces fine-grained admin roles; this work is to align invite controls with RBAC roles and ensure auditability for compliance customers.
scope: Server-side invite enforcement and audit logging. Deliverables: API middleware for invite rate-limits per admin identity and per-org burst windows; domain reputation evaluation against both tenant-configured allowlist/denylist and central global denylist; structured audit events for each invite action including decision_reason and policy_version; alert rule prototype in Console for flagging high invite rates.
out_of_scope: Console UI for configuring nuanced policies (separate Design ticket). Backend-side machine-learning based domain scoring (future work). Dedicated capacity integration edge cases for private deployments will be handled in follow-up if needed.
acceptance_criteria: Invite endpoint enforces per-admin rate limits (default 300 invites/day, configurable via org policy)
Burst protection enforces short window caps (e.g., 50 invites in 10 minutes) and returns clear 429 with mitigation guidance
Domain checks consult tenant allowlist/denylist, then global denylist, and mark invites failing reputation with reason codes
Audit log entries created for every invite attempt with fields: actor_id, actor_role, invitee_email, invite_result, decision_reason, policy_version
Automated unit and integration tests covering rate-limit windows and domain rules
Security review completed and threat-model updated with mitigation notes
tasks: Design API middleware for invite rate-limiting and integrate with RBAC v2 token context
Implement domain reputation service interface and adapter to tenant allowlist/denylist store
Add structured audit events and wire to existing audit pipeline (Kafka/topic: audit-invites)
Create alerting prototype script to surface sustain invite rate anomalies (SRE collaboration)
Write tests: unit, integration, and chaos test to validate burst handling
Prepare changelog notes and API contract update documentation
success_metrics: Reduction in org-level invite spikes (>100 invites/hour) by 95% in 30 days
Zero customer-reported mass-invite incidents after rollout
Audit events contain decision_reason and policy_version in 100% of invite actions
Latency added to invite endpoint < 15ms p99 attributable to checks

notes: Decision: default rate-limit values are conservative and configurable per-org. For SSO-only orgs, enforcement is stricter by default per security guidance.
Trade-off: performing domain reputation checks synchronously adds ~6-12ms; acceptable within SLOs but monitored. Consider async enrichment for lower-tier tenants later.
Follow-up: create a PM ticket to expose policy knobs in Console and a separate Ops runbook for responding to invite spike alerts.
